claim: This benchmark recovers ANNOTATION-DERIVED class labels (UniProtKB substrate/product annotations, via the SDR deposit) from sequence. It is not evidence about ketoreductase activity on any substrate, about the agent's selection logic, or about the pipeline's gates.

skipped_targets.sdr:substrate_cluster_6: 2 positive / 307 negative; 10 of each are required

similarity_to_training.measure: max k-mer cosine of a test sequence to any training-fold sequence
similarity_to_training.why_not: a k-mer cosine sits barely above its own composition background on this pool, and the folds promise an identity bound. Read grouping_audit for that

kernel_character.measure: median k-mer cosine between pool pairs, over the median between pairs of composition-preserving shuffles of the same sequences; no label is read

grouping_audit.identity_definition: global Needleman-Wunsch identity multiplied by the alignment coverage of the shorter sequence
grouping_audit.clustering_identity_definition: global Needleman-Wunsch identity multiplied by the alignment coverage of the shorter sequence

screens.name: kmer_jaccard>=0.05 (k=3)
screens.description: every cross-fold pair whose 3-mer Jaccard similarity is at least 0.05. The k-mer/identity relationship is monotone in practice but is not a bound, so a pair just under the screen can still be a true cluster-mate

grouping_audit.caveat: the grouping under audit aligned every pair, so no cross-cluster pair can be over the threshold and this audit cannot discover a leak. It is an independent check of the clustering code, not evidence about the grouping's design.

alignment_similarity.normalisation: bit score divided by the query profile's score against the query itself

spectrum_with_ridge.note: power-iteration estimates, not an exact spectrum; negative smallest means the matrix is not positive semi-definite and a ridge above its magnitude is what a Cholesky would need
